claims.claim: N4 consumes only frozen N2 at hash c6a65dc8d15f3c8e7e5b8d475bf6925a0b6028421adf84f927da361349da85a2. Every N2 payoff is transported to current R1 units with beta exactly once; no N3 or historical artifact is an input.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 1-2 and every interface source/payoff-date field.

claims.claim: Because weak proposers and weak voters cannot condition on theta, their positive-probability actions have the same conditional distribution under every remaining H type. Bayes therefore makes weak actions uninformative on path. This derived lemma imposes no restriction on exact zero-probability proposals or vote vectors.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 2 and 4; interface belief_system fields.

claims.claim: No pure H-ballot separating branch survives at 0<nu<1, whether every weak voter says yes or a weak no already blocks passage. Low-only current passage survives only at nu=0; positive-prior outcomes are pooling passage or deliberate delay.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 5 and the six branch classifications.

claims.claim: Delay support is exhausted by H rejection with all weak yes, or weak rejection with H yes. Exactly one weak rejector is strict and stage-undominated whenever x_j<g(nu), at every prior and every m>=2. Two or more weak rejectors survive exactly when nu<nu_2. T^Y removes genuine equality.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 3 and 8.2; each interface weak_nonproposer_ballot field.

claims.claim: For m=2 the exact support lower bound is L2(nu)=max{k2,min[z,(1-nu)q2]}. Whenever x<a0, weak rejection plus nonpivotal off-path low-H-no/high-H-yes separation yields only s=(1-nu)z. For x>=a0, endpoint/high rejection and forced passage establish the two binding guarantees e2 and k2.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 6; m=2 interface zero_probability fields; executable reviewer-counterexample regression.

claims.claim: Since L2<=p, m=2 pooling exists at every prior. Delay exists if and only if k2<=g(nu). At nu=0 low-only passage also always exists. Hence the prior candidate's m=2 none cell is refuted.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 6.3, 8, and 11; interface admissibility and existence fields.

claims.claim: For m>=3 the exact lower support bound is L3(nu)=s(nu)=(1-nu)z. Two weak no votes permit nonpivotal off-path H separation after every null proposal, assigning pooling N2 after the true low type and low-only N2 after the true high type. Conditional N2 minima and a forced-failure package prove the matching lower guarantee.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 7; m>=3 interface zero_probability fields.

claims.claim: For m>=3 both pooling and delay exist at every prior. In particular, the on-path exactly-one-weak-rejector construction survives at high priors and is distinct from the off-path two-rejector/nonpivotal-H-separation punishment.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 7-8; interface local_option_set and weak ballot fields; high-prior reviewer regression.

claims.claim: Within each proposer identity and accepted branch, every package in support has a common proposer payoff and common tie-break-minimal expected H payoff, equivalently common Y_i. The m=2 endpoint equality is open only when it necessarily uses the lower-H endpoint response; every retained pooling lower-bound equality requires the threshold offer.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 8.1 and every interface selection_status field.

claims.claim: The only within-identity cross-branch proposal mixtures are low-only/delay at nu=0 with (R_i,Y_i)=(a0,beta*o_0), and pooling/delay at nu>nu_2 with (R_i,Y_i)=(z,beta*o_1), subject to the m=2 delay condition. Low-only/pooling and low-region pooling/delay ties are removed by the lower-H proposal tie-break.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 9; endpoint and high-cell local option sets.

claims.claim: Different recognized proposer identities may select different local branches and null-history response maps. The interface preserves the full Cartesian product inside one global assessment and never recombines beliefs, outcomes, or payoffs ex post across assessments.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 2 and 9; every strategy_profile proposal_mixing field.

claims.claim: The lambda-indexed formulas retain proposer identity, asymmetric weak allocations, final N2 outcomes, and delay incidence. In the low N2 region final failure is D*nu; at nu=0 and in the high N2 region final passage with H is one. Passage without H is impossible under unanimity.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 10 and every interface payoff/outcome field.

claims.claim: P0 is refuted as a universal full-pie statement. Moving slack to r_i changes the exact proposal and may trigger a different pointwise ballot belief and punishment; accepted and delayed maximizing packages with strict budget slack survive.
claims.evidence: Derivation Section 11; interface set-valued support and slack statements.

claims.claim: The six cells partition m=2 versus m>=3 and nu=0, 0<nu<=nu_2, and nu_2<nu<=1. Every cell exists and there is no none cell. The complete correspondence is set-valued and does not deliver universal delay, screening, uniqueness, or a single informational-rent formula.
claims.evidence: Derivation Sections 8-11; six complete interface records; executable coverage classifier.
